title: Electrostatic Force Magnitude
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be correctly calculated as 1.5 × 10⁻³ N.

title: Ball A Charge
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be correctly calculated as +3 × 10⁻⁹ C.

title: Force Balance Setup
description: Important: The student must resolve forces on ball A into vertical (tension vs. weight) and horizontal (tension vs. electrostatic) components.

title: Correct Distance Calculation
description: Important: The student must correctly compute the separation r = l sin θ = 0.06 m using the geometry of the setup.

title: Coulomb's Law Application
description: Important: The student must apply Coulomb's law F = k|q_A q_B|/r² to relate the electrostatic force to the unknown charge q_A.

title: Sign of Charge
description: Optional: The student may note that the charges must be like (both positive or both negative) to produce repulsion, and the answer should include a positive sign.

title: Unit Consistency
description: Optional: The student may show proper unit conversion (cm to m, etc.) and dimensional analysis throughout the solution.

title: Incorrect Force Ratio
description: Pitfall: Using sin θ or cos θ incorrectly in the force balance (e.g., writing F = mg sin θ instead of F = mg tan θ).

title: Distance Mistake
description: Pitfall: Using an incorrect separation (e.g., r = l, r = l cos θ, or forgetting to convert length to meters).

title: Algebraic or Arithmetic Error
description: Pitfall: Making a calculation mistake in solving for q_A from Coulomb's law after obtaining F and r.
